title: Captivity
full_review:
"Captivity" (Lionsgate/After Dark) is a nasty film experience.

Most audiences will want to leave fairly early in the film. Elisha Cuthbert plays a model who is abducted and subjected to unrelenting torture by a masked figure for half the running time. By the time that some more interesting elements and twists come into the film, it is too late. Most audiences will have given up.

Its domestic release was dogged by controversy when a series of large billboards in Los Angeles showing the steps in the model's captivity were considered too graphic and were removed.

The main surprise is that the film (a U.S. co-production with Mosfilms, Moscow, and intended as a groundbreaker in collaboration) was directed by Roland Joffe, who had begun his career with "The Killing Fields" and "The Mission." He is a long, long way from those achievements, despite the publicity for the film constantly referring to his being a man "of vision and profound philosophy." He gives the film a glossy treatment and style but to little avail.

At one stage, the man in captivity with the model calls out (ironically, as it turns out) to the tormenter, "You twisted sicko freak." He well might be referring to the filmmakers or anyone unhappy enough to be watching.

The film contains graphic sex, violence, sadism and torture. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
